title: Preparation of Monodomain Liquid Crystal Elastomers and Liquid Crystal Elastomer Nanocomposites
protocol: Combine 166.23 mg of reactive mesogen with 40 mg of poly(hydromethylsiloxane) and 12.8 mg of crosslinker in a small vial containing 0.6 ml of anhydrous toluene.
Stir the solution at 35 °C for 25 min to dissolve.
Prepare a solution of 1 wt % dichloro(1,5-cyclooctadiene)-platinum(II) catalyst in dichloromethane.
Add 30 µl of catalyst solution to the reagents via pipette.
Stir to mix thoroughly.
Pour the solution into a custom-made rectangular polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) mold.
Cover the mold loosely with a glass slide and place in heating oven at 60 °C for 30 min while shaking periodically to remove bubbles during the first 15 min.
Remove mold from heating oven and cool with liquid nitrogen by pouring liquid nitrogen into a small container and contacting the bottom of the PTFE mold with the liquid nitrogen for 2 sec.
Carefully remove elastomer from mold using a metal spatula and place on top of a PTFE sheet.
Trim the edges of the LCE using a razor blade.
Cut the LCE along its length into three equal sized pieces (approx. 2.7 cm length and 0.5 cm width).
Hang each piece by one end to a horizontal rod and attach paperclips to the other end.
Hold the LCE in place using tape.
Add paperclips one at a time in 10 min increments.
Hang the LCE for 7 days at room temperature, noting changes in length and uniformity.
Discard any sample that tears or breaks.
Remove samples and store at ambient temperature.
Repeat steps 1.1 to 1.4 above.
Add 4.38 mg carbon black nanoparticles to the reaction solution containing reactive mesogen, crosslinker, and siloxane.
Use a total of 5 paperclips for loading.
Prepare 1% w/v solution of carbon black nanoparticles in toluene.
Sonicate for 20 min to disperse nanoparticles.
Pour the dispersion into a Petri dish.
Immerse LCEs from step 2.1 in nanoparticle dispersion for 6 hr.
Withdraw the solution from the Petri dish with a pipette.
Allow the elastomer to dry in air.
Gently clean excess carbon particles on the surface using tape or cotton swab.
Mix 246.15 mg of 4,4'-diglycidyloxybiphenyl-3,101 mg sebacic acid, 71.6 mg hexadecanedioic acid, and 76 mg carboxydecyl-terminated polydimethylsiloxane in a custom-made PTFE mold.
Heat the samples by placing on a hotplate at 180 °C.
Add 11.48 mg of (1,5,7-triazabicyclo[4.4.0] dec-5-ene) catalyst and stir using metal tweezers pre-heated to 180 °C.
Continue reacting until the mixture forms a gel after approximately 20 min, stirring periodically to remove bubbles generated by the reaction.
Remove the PTFE boat from the hotplate and allow to cool to RT.
Use a razor blade to separate the elastomer from the PTFE mold.
Place two PTFE sheets in a polymer press at 180 °C.
Place the elastomer between the PTFE sheets and compress the sample to a thickness of 0.3 - 0.5 mm.
Continue heating at 180 °C for 4 hr.
Remove the sample and cool to RT.
Cut the sample into rectangular pieces (approximately 2.5 cm length and 0.5 cm width).
Hang the sample at one end using polyimide tape inside a heating oven.
Attach 12 paperclips (8.88 g) to the free end of the sample.
Set the temperature of the heating oven to 165 °C O/N, or for 12 - 16 hr.
Remove the elastomer from the heating oven and note the change in length.
Heat the sample to 80 °C on a hotplate to remove residual stress then cool back to RT.
Heat the samples on a hotplate to 120 °C.
Image the heated samples with a camera.
Note the initial sample length at room temperature (RT).
Record the sample length after heating to 120 °C.
Measure the sample length after cooling back to RT.
Analyze phase transition temperature and glass transition by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) from 0 °C to 150 °C at a rate of 10 °C/min.
Quantify the degree of liquid crystal alignment by X-ray diffraction measurements.
Place samples in an X-ray diffractometer with 2D imaging capabilities.
Measure stiffness and changes in length and width using dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA).
Record length and stiffness changes as a function of temperature for LCEs.
Fasten manually cut samples to dimensions of 2 cm x 0.3 cm between tension clamps.
Apply a force of 1 mN to remove any slack from the samples.
Thermally equilibrate samples at 30 °C followed by heating and cooling cycles at 5 °C/min.
Heat sample from 30 °C up to 120 °C.
Manually cut LCE nanocomposite samples to dimensions of 2 cm x 0.3 cm.
Glue a copper wire at opposite ends of the LCE nanocomposites using silver epoxy.
Fasten the LCE nanocomposite using tension clamps with 1 mN tension.
Apply an electrical potential through the copper wires at a voltage ranging from 0 - 60 V, a frequency of 60 Hz, and an on/off pulse duration ranging from 0.1 sec - 30 sec.
Record shape changes in response to the electrical potential.
Treat one surface of LCE nanocomposites under oxygen plasma for 30 sec.
Spin cast 300 µl of a solution of polystyrene in toluene (1% w/v) at 3,300 rpm for 1 min on top of the plasma cleaned surface.
Dry the elastomer under vacuum for 12 hr to remove toluene.
Treat the polystyrene-coated surface of the LCE nanocomposite using oxygen plasma for 30 sec.
Place LCE nanocomposites in a 70% ethanol solution for 30 minutes to sterilize the surface.
Wash the LCE nanocomposite with phosphate-buffered saline.
Transfer the LCE to a dry Petri dish with the polystyrene-coated side facing up.
Immerse the entire surface of the LCE in 5 ml of a rat tail collagen type I solution (50 µg/ml in 0.02 N acetic acid).
Incubate the LCE nanocomposite at 37 °C and 5% CO₂ for at least 30 minutes.
Isolate neonatal rat ventricular cardiomyocytes and suspend them in high-serum plating media as previously reported.
Plate cells on top of LCE substrates described above at a density of 100,000 - 600,000 cells/cm².
Around 24 hours later, transfer the cells to low serum maintenance media (DMEM, 18.5% M199, 5% HS, 1% FBS and antibiotics).
Allow cardiomyocytes to attach and proliferate on the surface of the LCE for 4 days.
Design and fabricate a custom vessel using a 3-D printer according to the manufacturer's protocol.
Insert carbon rods through the holes across the vessels.
Hold the carbon rods in place using medical grade silicone adhesive.
Cure the adhesive overnight.
Transfer LCE nanocomposites with cardiomyocytes to the custom 3D-printed vessel filled with cell culture maintenance media.
Place the LCE across the carbon rods.
Fix one end of the LCE to ensure electrical contact.
Insert a rectangular plastic piece loosely over the LCE sample through the notches in the 3-D vessel.
Apply a 40 V AC electrical potential to electrically stimulate the LCE with a 5 sec on/off time for a total of 24 hr.
Stain the membrane of living cells using Calcein AM as described previously.
Cover the cells with DAPI-containing mounting medium before imaging under an inverted fluorescent microscope.
Use ImageJ to count the number of living cells.
Determine the angle of cell alignment using the best fit function.
Repeat steps involving electrically and thermally stimulating LCE without carbon black nanoparticles added.
Transfer the LCE with cardiomyocytes to a Petri dish containing maintenance media and a Kapton resistive heater.
Supply heat to the LCE by turning on the resistive heater at 12 W heating power.
Cycle on and off the heat with 5 sec intervals for at least 24 hr.
